summary: A deep clone must create every reachable vertex and reproduce every adjacency entry, imposing an output-size lower bound of Omega(V + E). The identity-map traversal matches that bound.

optimality.argument: The returned deep copy contains V newly allocated node objects and the same E undirected edges, represented by 2E neighbor entries. Producing those objects and references requires Omega(V + E) work. The current traversal maps each vertex once and processes every adjacency entry once, giving O(V + E) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Every original vertex needs a distinct clone, and every original neighbor relationship must appear in the cloned adjacency, so none of the V vertices or E edges can be omitted.
The identity map creates one clone per reached vertex, and each neighbor-list entry triggers one constant-time map lookup plus one append.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a cycle, one isolated node, and an empty graph; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
